results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Resonating Lute, Inevitable Defeat and Jeskai Revelation.
results.text:
The deck is accepted. It's a four-color brew: Jeskai control with a black splash, built around Resonating Lute.

**The plan.** Early on you survive with cheap interaction: 4 Lightning Helix, 2 Burst Lightning, 2 Get Lost, 4 No More Lies, Spell Snare and 2 Day of Judgment. On turn 4 you land Resonating Lute. After that, every land taps for two mana of any one color for instants and sorceries. With five lands that's 10 mana, so you can cast Jeskai Revelation (7 mana) on turn 5 and still hold up 3 mana. A turn later you can cast Revelation and Inevitable Defeat in the same turn. Inevitable Defeat can't be countered: it exiles their best permanent and drains 3 life. Revelation bounces a threat, deals 4 damage, makes two prowess Monks, draws two cards and gains you 4 life. Consult the Star Charts and Stock Up keep your hand at seven or more cards, which is when Lute's own tap ability starts drawing you an extra card each turn. You win by chaining Revelations, with the Monks, burn and the Defeat drains closing it out.

**The three directions I sketched:**
1. **Jeskai Control with a black splash (chosen).** It's built on a recent 5-0 Jeskai Control list that already plays 3 Lute and 3 Revelation. Separately, Inevitable Defeat shows up in 118 published lists alongside Lightning Helix, Get Lost and Revelation, so these cards already live together in the same shell.
2. **Mardu control.** Dropping blue isn't possible, because Lute and Revelation both need it.
3. **The Lessons/spellslinger package from the menu.** Lute showed up in one Lessons list, but that deck's cheap red/blue spells do nothing for a 4-mana Mardu removal spell.

I picked the first because Lute does two jobs there at once: it ramps you to Revelation, and its "any one color" mana fixes the black for Inevitable Defeat.

**How the mana handles the fourth color.** The deck runs 4 Great Hall of the Biblioplex, which can make any color for instants and sorceries if you pay 1 life. Add Godless Shrine, Blood Crypt and Watery Grave and you have 8 black sources before Lute comes down. Against the Jeskai Control lists, land count and colored sources came out in line; the checker raised no warnings.

**The honest odds:**
- You'll have Lute by turn 5 on the play in about 57% of games.
- The full five-card line is complete by turn 8 in only about 8.6% of games. That number counts every piece, though, and in practice any Revelation or Defeat after Lute does the job.
- I left out Opt and Sleight of Hand on purpose. They keep your hand the same size, but Lute only draws when you hold seven cards, so the deck runs card-gain spells instead.

The sideboard is aimed at the current top decks:
- **Against Prowess and Elementals:** Fire Magic (an instant, so Lute mana pays for it), Pyroclasm and Seam Rip.
- **Against the counterspell and Omniscience decks:** Tishana's Tidebinder, Disdainful Stroke, Negate and Voice of Victory.
- **Against graveyard decks:** Rest in Peace.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around The Jolly Balloon Man, Sewer-veillance Cam and Bloom Tender.
results.text:
This is a four-color (white, blue, red, green) infinite combo brew. The submission was accepted on the second try: the checker flagged format staples I wasn't playing, so I swapped 3 Spell Pierce for 3 Opt and moved 2 Spell Pierce to the sideboard.

**The plan:** The Jolly Balloon Man pays {1} to make hasty token copies of your creatures, and the deck loops that ability using two Merfolk.
1. Have Forensic Researcher on the battlefield. Balloon Man copies it, and the hasty Researcher token taps to untap Balloon Man.
2. Balloon Man copies Deepway Navigator. The token's enter-the-battlefield trigger untaps every other Merfolk, including all your Researcher tokens.
3. One Researcher token untaps Balloon Man. A second one untaps Bloom Tender, which taps for 3–4 mana (it makes one mana per color among your permanents: white, blue, green and red).
4. Each loop costs {1} and gives back more than that. You get infinite mana and infinite hasty 1/1 flying Navigator tokens, which become 2/1s once three Merfolk attack. Attack for lethal.

**The three cards you asked for:**
- **Sewer-veillance Cam** untaps Balloon Man when it enters and again when it leaves, so it saves a step or mana while setting up the loop. Otherwise it untaps Bloom Tender for extra mana, and sacrificing it draws two cards to find a missing piece.
- **Bloom Tender** is your ramp and color fixing, and it's the engine that makes the loop produce surplus mana. Even without it the loop still works using a land, it just doesn't make extra mana.
- **Balloon Man** copying Formidable Speaker gives a hasty tutor for whichever piece you're missing.

**The quickest kill is turn 4:** Bloom Tender on turn 2, Researcher on turn 3, then Navigator plus Balloon Man and two activations on turn 4. Neither the Researcher nor the Navigator you cast needs to have been around since your last turn.

**How often it comes together:** By turn 5 you've drawn Balloon Man, Navigator and a Researcher or Speaker naturally in about 24% of games. Speaker's tutor and Opt push that higher, but the deck's real job is to survive with Burst Lightning and Get Lost until the pieces line up. Instant-speed sweepers and removal on Balloon Man are its biggest weaknesses.

**Directions I considered:**
1. This Merfolk untap loop.
2. A Selesnya Offense / Aang creature shell that splashes blue for Cam and uses Balloon Man to copy enter-the-battlefield creatures like Brightglass Gearhulk.
3. A Blink-style Azorius value deck.

I chose the loop because it's the only direction that turns all three of your cards into a game-winning line instead of just value. I still borrowed the Aang decks' green-white mana pieces (Temple Garden, Hushwood Verge, Llanowar Elves).

The sideboard is aimed at Prowess and Lessons (Flashfreeze, Lightning Helix, Seam Rip), control (Disdainful Stroke, Spell Pierce) and graveyard decks (Rest in Peace).

1. A Dwarf/Equipment deck built around Mauler, using Boros Aggro's cheap burn and land count.
2. A slower Dwarf tokens build around Fíli the Pathfinder.
3. Dwarves mixed into the Boros Weapons artifact shell.

I picked the first. The three cards you asked for all do the most when the deck is dense with cheap Dwarves and Equipment. Boros Weapons is an artifact control deck that plays almost no creatures, so I only borrowed its Boros dual lands.

- **Backup double strike:** Giott and Dáin Ironfoot also give double strike, so equipped creatures besides Mauler still hit hard.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Greedy Freebooter, The Sackville-Bagginses and Umbral Collar Zealot.
results.text:
I built an Orzhov (white-black) sacrifice deck, which I'm calling a brew. No published list in the last 400 days plays your three cards together, so there was no deck to copy.

**The plan:** Greedy Freebooter, Bloodghast and Voice of Victory give you creatures to sacrifice. Tolls of War makes a Clue token and then a 1/1 Ally token on each of your turns that you sacrifice something. Umbral Collar Zealot is the free sacrifice outlet. The Sackville-Bagginses makes the opponent lose 1 life every time you sacrifice a token, and that includes Treasures you spend for mana. Sephiroth, Popular Egotist and Vito add more life drain on top of combat damage. The deck should take over around turn 5 or 6.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **Mono-black:** Sephiroth, Popular Egotist and Gas Guzzler. Gas Guzzler only works once its speed counter is maxed out, so it's slow, and this version has no source of tokens for Sackville to drain off.
2. **Rakdos (black-red):** Sawblade Skinripper and Zhao, borrowing Bloodghast from Mardu Discard. It has good payoffs but makes few tokens.
3. **Orzhov, using Mardu Discard's mana and two of its cards (chosen):** Tolls of War, Voice of Victory and Vito all turn sacrifices into tokens and drain. That gives Sackville the most to work with, so I picked this one.

**How the cards work together:**
- **Voice of Victory and Sackville:** Voice's two attack tokens are sacrificed at end of turn anyway. With Sackville out, each one drains 1, or you can feed them to the Zealot first. Voice also stops opponents from casting spells during your turn.
- **Requiting Hex and Freebooter:** Hex lets you put a -1/-1 counter on your own creature to gain 2 life. Putting it on a Freebooter kills it, so you still get the Treasure and the scry.
- **Bitter Triumph and Bloodghast:** Triumph's extra cost can be discarding a card. Discard Bloodghast and it comes back on your next land drop.
- **Mana:** I borrowed the Godless Shrine, Concealed Courtyard and Starting Town base from Mardu Discard, with 22 lands. The deck check's only complaint was that it has fewer red sources than Mardu Discard, which doesn't matter since this deck plays no red cards.

**Card counts:** Sackville and Sephiroth are at 3 copies and Vito at 2 because they're legendary, and a second copy in play would have to go to the graveyard.

**Win odds:** Drawing every card in the win line by turn 6 is only about 0.3%. That number just reflects how many different cards the line names. In practice the fodder, sacrifice outlets and drain cards back each other up, so you rarely need that exact set.

Seam Rip is in the sideboard rather than the main deck, for matchups like Prowess and Landfall where most threats cost 2 or less.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Gideon's Memorial, Solitary Cell and Ajani Unrelenting.
results.text:
This is a Boros (red-white) superfriends tokens brew. No published list has ever played these three cards together, so it's built from scratch. The mana base and cheap removal come from Boros Dragons.

**The three directions I considered:**
1. **Boros planeswalkers + tokens.** Gideon's Memorial ramps into planeswalkers and makes tokens bigger. Ajani Unrelenting's −3 deals 4 damage to every creature except your tokens, so it clears their board and leaves yours.
2. **Jeskai planeswalker control.** This is how Ajani Unrelenting actually gets played, alongside Chandra, Stock Up and Day of Judgment. But the Memorial's token boost would do nothing there.
3. **Borrow the Boros Dragons package** (Sarkhan, Voice of Victory). The dragons aren't tokens, so Ajani's −3 would kill your own board.

**I chose direction 1** because it's the only one where all three requested cards make each other better.

**The plan:**
- **Turn 2:** Gideon's Memorial. It gives your tokens +1/+0 and vigilance, and its mana can only be spent on planeswalkers.
- **Turn 3:** Ajani, Outland Chaperone, which makes 1/1 tokens with +1 and deals 4 to a tapped creature with −2.
- **Turn 4:** Elspeth, Storm Slayer a turn early, using the Memorial's mana. From then on she doubles every token you make.
- **Turn 5:** Ajani Unrelenting. Its −3 wipes their creatures and keeps your tokens. Every loyalty ability you use makes a 2/2 Cadet token (two with Elspeth out).
- **Turn 6:** Ajani's +1 gives everything +1/+0 and haste. Because the Memorial gives tokens vigilance, they can attack and still guard your planeswalkers.

Solitary Cell is your 2-mana removal against Jund Sacrifice, Elementals and Landfall threats costing 3 or less. Later it turns extra legendary cards (spare Memorials, an Ajani you can't cast yet) into fresh draws.

**Honest odds:** the exact four-card line above is fully drawn by turn 6 in only about 6% of games. In practice the deck swaps pieces in: Chandra, Hop to It and Voice of Victory fill in for the specific planeswalkers. You'll see a Memorial or a Cell by turn 6 about 85% of the time, but Ajani Unrelenting only about half the time. I run 3 Ajanis because it's a 6-mana legendary, and a second copy can be discarded to the Cell to draw a card.

**Sideboard:** aimed at the current field. Rest in Peace for Reanimator and graveyard decks, Seam Rip and Pyroclasm for cheap threats from Elementals and Prowess, and Dawn's Truce to protect your board from removal.

results.prompt: Brew me a Pioneer deck built around Slumbering Trudge, Fight Rigging and The Great Henge.
results.text:
I built a Golgari brew: **"Trudge Stompy," Pioneer**. In Pioneer, Slumbering Trudge costs {X}{G}. If you cast it for X=0, it's a 6/6 for one green mana. It comes in tapped with 3 stun counters, so it can't attack or block for a few turns. That doesn't matter much, because the deck uses its power, not its attacks:
- **The Great Henge** costs {7}{G}{G} minus our biggest creature's power. With Trudge out it costs just {1}{G}{G}.
- **Fight Rigging** puts a +1/+1 counter on Trudge at the start of combat. That takes it to 7 power, which lets us play the card hidden under Fight Rigging for free.

**The plan:** Turn 1 a mana elf. Turn 2 Badgermole Cub plus a cheap Trudge. Turn 3 Henge for three mana, then Fight Rigging off Henge's own {G}{G}. After that, every creature draws a card. Ouroboroid pumps the whole team, Ghalta, Primal Hunger drops to {G}{G}, and Fight Rigging can play Craterhoof Behemoth for free. Fatal Push, Thoughtseize and Abrupt Decay hold off the opponent until then.

**Odds:** You'll have Trudge, a dork and Henge or Fight Rigging all by turn 3 in about 23% of games. A 6+ power creature plus Henge or Fight Rigging by turn 4 happens about 49% of the time. In other games, Ouroboroid or a pile of elves supplies the power more slowly. The checker reported a 0% chance of drawing every card in the win line by turn 5. That's expected: the line lists alternatives (Ouroboroid, Ghalta or Craterhoof), and you only need one of them.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **Mono-green stompy**, using the elves and Cub from the Selesnya and Golgari lists.
2. **Selesnya with Collected Company.** Company can put Trudge into play, but it can't find Henge or Fight Rigging.
3. **Golgari**, borrowing Golgari Midrange's mana and cheap black removal (17% of the field). **I chose this one**: the menu's elves and Cub package already powers the engine, and the black cards add the interaction mono-green lacks.

**Things to know:**
- No published list plays all three of your cards together. The closest real decks are Modern "Fanatic Eldrazi" lists, which pair Trudge with Fight Rigging, but most of their key cards aren't legal in Pioneer.
- It runs 22 lands (counting the two Turntimber Symbiosis double-faced cards) plus 8 elves. That's below Golgari Midrange's 24, closer to Mono-Green Devotion's 21.
- Henge (3 copies) and Ghalta (2) are legendary, so I ran fewer than 4 to avoid stuck duplicates. Craterhoof is a single copy because Fight Rigging and Turntimber can also find it.
- I left out Sheoldred and Unholy Annex. They need heavier black than this light splash supports, and Henge already provides card draw. Culling Ritual is sideboard-only because it would destroy our own elves, Cub and Trudge.

**Sideboard:** aimed at the decks the meta shows: Golgari Midrange, Selesnya Company, Greasefang, the Prowess decks and UW Control.

results.text:
I built **Azorius Heroic around your three cards**, and the deck was accepted as legal. It's a brew that borrows its shell from the small Azorius Heroic archetype (3 recent lists).

**The plan:** Play Favored Hoplite on turn 1 and Illuminator Virtuoso on turn 2. Then cast cheap spells that target your own creatures, and each one adds a +1/+1 counter, triggers Hoplite's damage prevention, or makes Virtuoso connive (draw, discard, grow).
- **Guiding Voice** is a 1-mana counter that also triggers heroic. Its Learn then grabs a protection Lesson from the sideboard, like Enter the Avatar State or Octopus Form, so you protect the threat with a spell that wasn't even in your deck.
- **Practiced Offense** is the finisher. It puts a counter on every creature you control and gives double strike to a pumped Hoplite, or lifelink to Virtuoso, who already has double strike. Its flashback costs 2, so you can do it again later.
- **Slip Out the Back, Secret Identity and Sheltered by Ghosts** protect your creatures from Fatal Push and similar removal. Sheltered by Ghosts also exiles their best blocker.

The deck aims to win around turn 4, but that depends on drawing a creature plus the right mix of spells. Don't read the 0.7% from the checker as a win rate: it's the chance of drawing all six cards in my sample line by turn 4, and the deck only needs a few of them.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **Mono-White Heroic** (Lagonna-Band Trailblazer, Seasoned Hallowblade, Homestead Courage/Dig Site Inventory). The mana is cleaner, but it has almost no cheap protection.
2. **Boros heroic-prowess**, borrowing Monstrous Rage and Reckless Rage from Mono-Red Prowess. More damage, but the red pump spells don't protect anything.
3. **Azorius Heroic** (chosen). Against a field full of Fatal Push, Thoughtseize and Abrupt Decay, a heroic deck needs 1-mana protection most of all. Blue supplies it, and Guiding Voice adds more from the sideboard.

**Choices you might question:**
- **No green.** The real lists run a few green lands so Elusive Otter can also be cast as Grove's Bounty, its adventure side. I cut green for smoother mana: the Otter is always castable for blue, so the adventure is just a bonus I gave up. The checker flagged the missing green sources; this is why.
- **18 lands plus Sejiri Shelter**, which is a spell that can be played as a land. The real lists run about one more land than this. Your average spell costs 1.47, and Practiced Offense's flashback gives spare mana somewhere to go.
- **Two format staples skipped.** Stormchaser's Talent never targets your creatures, so it triggers none of the heroic effects. Boomerang Basics would bounce your own creature and lose its counters.
- **The sideboard** holds four Lessons for Learn (Enter the Avatar State, Octopus Form, Reduce to Memory, Airbender's Reversal). The rest targets the top decks:
  - Rest in Peace for Phoenix and Greasefang
  - Seam Rip for the prowess decks and Selesnya Company
  - Dovin's Veto for UW Control
  - Erode and Stormchaser Drake for the remaining matchups

results.text:
I built **4-Color Revelation Control**. It's a brew: white-blue-red with a small black splash.

**The plan:** Counter and remove everything early with No More Lies, Lightning Helix, Firebending Lesson, Get Lost, March of Otherworldly Light and Supreme Verdict. Tablet of Discovery does two jobs: it gives you an extra red mana, or two red mana for instants. With 5 lands plus Tablet you can cast Jeskai Revelation at the end of the opponent's turn 5. Each Revelation returns a permanent to its owner's hand, deals 4 damage, makes two Monk tokens, draws two cards and gains you 4 life. Inevitable Defeat can't be countered; it exiles their best permanent and drains 3. You win with Monks, The Wandering Emperor, Teferi, and the drain and burn. I listed turn 9 as the target, but this is a control deck, so it's a rough estimate.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **Port the Standard 4C Control deck.** Every real list running all three of your cards is that Standard deck (135 lists), built around Stock Up, Flashback, Sear and Day of Judgment.
2. **Add the cards to Pioneer's five-color Niv-Mizzet shell.** It already plays Lightning Helix, the three-color lands that enter tapped (triomes) and Supreme Verdict. But its green ramp and Bring to Light package would push your three cards to the side.
3. **Use Pioneer's UW Control package** (No More Lies, Consult the Star Charts, The Wandering Emperor, Teferi, March, Get Lost, Verdict). Add red and a small black splash for your cards, and borrow the Standard deck's engine of Tablet, Revelation and Helix.

**I chose direction 3.** It keeps your three cards at the center while running Pioneer's best proven counterspells and removal in these colors.

**Mana:** 26 lands plus 4 Tablets.
- White is the base, with 19 sources (UW Control averages about 20).
- There are 9 black sources for Inevitable Defeat. Great Hall of the Biblioplex counts as one, since its any-color mana only works for instants and sorceries, and both of your four-color spells are instants.
- `check_deck` found no issues.

**Choices worth knowing:**
- **Format staples I left out:** Thoughtseize and Fatal Push need black early, and black is only a splash here. The prowess creatures, Reckless Rage and Stormchaser's Talent don't fit a control plan.
- **A fourth Lightning Helix replaced Stock Up.** The submission tool requires 4 copies of any card in the win line. A fourth Helix also helps against prowess, which is 20% of the field.
- **The win-line odds look bad but aren't the real number.** The tool reports drawing every card in the line by turn 9 in only about 4% of games. That counts having all six specific cards at once. In practice you win with any mix of Revelations, Defeats and burn.

**Sideboard:**
- Dovin's Veto and Mystical Dispute for control and the Izzet decks.
- Rest in Peace and Kutzil's Flanker for Greasefang and Phoenix.
- Beza, Sear, Fire Magic, Farewell and a third Verdict for the creature decks.

results.text:
I've built a Boros Dragons brew around your three cards. No published list in any format plays all three together, so this is a new deck. I borrowed the shell from Standard's Boros Dragons. **The plan:** Momo comes down on turn 1. On turn 2, Sarkhan reveals a Dragon from your hand and makes a Treasure. That Treasure, plus Momo making your first flier each turn cost 1 less, gets you to a hasty Shivan Devastator, a Nova Hellkite cast for its cheaper "warp" cost of 3, or a Magmatic Hellkite a turn early. Every Dragon that enters gives Sarkhan a +1/+1 counter and flying for the turn. Lorehold arrives around turn 4 as a 5/5 flying, hasty threat. On each opponent's upkeep you may discard a card to draw one. If that draw is an instant or sorcery, you can cast it right then for {2} ("miracle"). That makes Lightning Helix, Get Lost and Lorehold Command (normally 5 mana) cheap to cast on the other player's turn. Burst Lightning clears blockers early and deals the last points of damage late.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **Boros Dragons midrange.** Borrows Standard's Dragon package (Momo, Clarion Conqueror, the Hellkites) plus Burst Lightning, which the Pioneer Prowess decks on your menu all run.
2. **Boros miracle control.** Uses Lorehold to cast expensive spells like Chandra's Ignition or Farewell for {2}.
3. **Red-heavy aggro.** A Prowess-style shell with the Dragons added on top.

**I chose direction 1.** Sarkhan needs a Dragon in hand on turn 2 to make his Treasure, so the deck has to be full of Dragons (17 of them). Miracle only works while Lorehold is on the battlefield and the spell is in your hand, so it should be a bonus, not the engine.

**Card choices:**
- **Clarion Conqueror** is a Dragon that also stops activated abilities. That shuts down Greasefang's Parhelion crew, Professor Dellian Fel and Llanowar Elves. The catch: it also stops you from using Sarkhan's Treasure, so cast it after you've spent the Treasure.
- **Voice of Victory** stops opponents from casting spells during your turn, which helps against UW Control and Lessons.

**Things to know:**
- **Copies:** I run 3 Lorehold because it's legendary and costs 5. Sarkhan and Shivan Devastator run 4 each.
- **Odds:** You'll have Sarkhan plus a Dragon to reveal by turn 2 in about 41% of games (with no mulligans). You'll have some Dragon in hand about 94% of the time.
- **Mana:** The checker suggests about 24 lands; I run 23, so a 24th land is a reasonable change.
- **Fragility:** The deck leans on creatures, so Golgari's removal and sweepers from control are the real tests.

The 15-card sideboard is aimed at the decks the meta shows most: Rest in Peace and Exorcise for Greasefang and Cauldron, and Magebane Lizard and Fiery Impulse for the Prowess decks.

results.prompt: Brew me a Modern deck built around Eyetwitch, Stitcher's Supplier and Flare of Malice.
results.text:
I built a Rakdos Archon reanimator brew around your three cards. No published list in the last 400 days plays all three together. However, the Modern Reanimator deck already runs Stitcher's Supplier (3.9 copies on average) and Flare of Malice (4 copies) in all 17 recent lists, so I borrowed its shell and mana.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **Rakdos Reanimator with Archon of Cruelty and Persist (chosen).** Eyetwitch replaces the non-black filler (Detective's Phoenix, Voldaren Epicure).
2. **Grixis Persist with Psychic Frog.** Supplier and Eyetwitch would be the cheap bodies.
3. **Rakdos sacrifice deck with Goblin Bombardment and Bloodghast.** Flare would just be removal.

I picked the first because every card in it helps the others. In that shell, Eyetwitch stops being a weak 1/1 and becomes a free way to get Archon into the graveyard.

**How the three cards work together**
- **Flare of Malice:** you can sacrifice a nontoken black creature instead of paying its 4 mana. The opponent then sacrifices their biggest creature or planeswalker. That answers big threats like Phlage or Devourer of Destiny for 0 mana. The deck has 16 black creatures you can sacrifice to it.
- **Eyetwitch:** when it dies, you may discard a card to draw a card. Sacrificing it to Flare (or to Village Rites or Corrupted Conviction) kills their best creature, lets you discard Archon and draws you a replacement.
- **Stitcher's Supplier:** mills 3 cards when it enters and 3 more when it dies. That fills the graveyard with Archon and Bloodghast, and Supplier is also something to sacrifice to Flare.

**The win line:** Get Archon into the graveyard with Eyetwitch, Faithless Looting or Supplier, then bring it back on turn 2 or 3 with Persist (2 mana). Emperor of Bones is a second way to bring it back. Each time Archon enters or attacks, the opponent sacrifices a creature, discards and loses 3 life, while you draw and gain 3. Flare, Fatal Push and Lightning Bolt clear the way.

**Odds and other details:**
- Seeing Persist, Archon and a discard card (Looting or Eyetwitch) together by turn 3 on the draw is about 20% with no help. Supplier's mill, Village Rites and Corrupted Conviction raise that, though I didn't calculate by how much.
- The checker's 1.2% is the chance of drawing all six cards named in the line by turn 5, which the deck doesn't actually need.
- There are 18 lands, the same as the real Reanimator lists.
- The sideboard is the Reanimator deck's standard set, aimed at Energy, Affinity and Living End.

**Watch out:** Vexing Bauble, which the deck sideboards and many opponents also run, counters free spells, and that includes a Flare cast by sacrificing a creature.

**The plan:** Slumbering Trudge is a 6/6 for one green mana if you cast it with X=0. It comes in tapped with three stun counters, but its power is all the deck needs. At the start of your combat, Fight Rigging puts a +1/+1 counter on it, which brings it to 7 power. That lets you play the card Rigging hid for free: The Great Henge, Craterhoof Behemoth, Ouroboroid or Turntimber Symbiosis. Trudge being out also does several other jobs:
- **Fanatic of Rhonas** taps for four green mana instead of one (five with Badgermole Cub).
- **The Great Henge** costs only three green mana.
- **Life's Legacy** can sacrifice Trudge to draw six cards.
- **Quirion Ranger** untaps Trudge, which removes a stun counter.

That extra mana pays for Turntimber Symbiosis's seven-mana spell side. It puts a creature onto the battlefield, and Ouroboroid or Trudge comes in with three extra counters. On any other turn Turntimber is just a land.

**Win line:** Turn 1 Ignoble Hierarch, turn 2 Fight Rigging, turn 3 Trudge, and then the free card at combat. From there, Henge card draw or Craterhoof should finish the game around turn 5.

**Honest odds:** You'll have Fight Rigging and Trudge (or Green Sun's Zenith to fetch it) together by turn 4 on the play only 40.5% of the time. In other games the deck plays as green stompy: Trudge, Fanatic and Henge still work without Rigging.

1. **Mono-green Trudge/Henge ramp:** borrows the package from the real Trudge lists. This is the one I chose.
2. **Summoner's Pact toolbox:** taken from the menu's Neoform and Amulet Titan decks.
3. **Red-green with Energy's burn:** Galvanic Discharge for removal.

I picked option 1 because only that one gives Trudge's cheap power more than one payoff at once. Options 2 and 3 would make Trudge and Rigging extra cards rather than the engine.

**Choices worth knowing:**
- **Copy counts:** 3 Great Henge, since it's legendary and can also be hidden by Rigging. Craterhoof is a single copy because Green Sun's Zenith and Turntimber can find it.
- **No Mishra's Bauble:** it's a popular card in green, but it adds no power or mana, and every slot here goes to that.
- **Interaction:** 3 Dismember and 2 Endurance in the main deck. The sideboard is aimed at Affinity, Storm, Living End and Goryo's Vengeance.

I built a Dimir artifact storm deck, "Riddlesmith Storm." It's a brew that borrows its mana base and its free-artifact package from The Epic Storm (TES). You discard Daredevil, and when the artifact enters, Daredevil comes back to your hand. So every artifact you cast nets you a card. The deck runs 19 free artifacts (Lotus Petal, Chrome Mox, Mox Opal, Lion's Eye Diamond, Mishra's Bauble), and each one adds a storm count and digs deeper.

When your hand runs dry, crack Lion's Eye Diamond with Echo of Eons in hand (or discard Echo to a Riddlesmith loot). Then flash Echo back for {2}{U} to draw a fresh seven in the middle of the turn. Echo refills the opponent's hand too, so only use it on the turn you go off. Finish with Infernal Tutor once your hand is empty (it then finds any card) or with Wishclaw Talisman. Either one finds Tendrils of Agony, which drains 20 or more at storm count 9. The goal is to win on turn 3 or 4.

**Why this direction:**
- **What I compared:**
  - Blue Affinity (Saga, Emry, Kappa Cannoneer): Echo of Eons would mostly sit dead there.
  - Grixis graveyard midrange like Modern's Asmo Food (the only real decks running Daredevil): Riddlesmith and Echo would be weak there.
- **Why storm won:** It's the only plan where all three cards do a real job. Riddlesmith needs lots of cheap artifacts, Daredevil needs both looting and artifacts entering, and Echo needs a cheap way into the graveyard plus a reason to refill mid-turn.

**Things to know:**
- **Consistency:** You'll find a Riddlesmith by turn 3 in about 49% of games, but both engine pieces together only about 22% of the time. When the engine doesn't come together, the deck plays as a leaner TES: rituals, Diamond, Infernal Tutor. The submit check reported a 0% chance of naturally drawing all eight cards in the kill sequence by turn 4. That number ignores tutors and looting, but take it as a sign that this deck is much less consistent than stock TES.

results.text:
I built **Grixis Ritual Phoenix**, a brew. It turns Buried Alive into a fast combo kill.

**How it wins:** Cast Dark Ritual for three black mana, then Buried Alive to put three Arclight Phoenix in your graveyard. Then cast one more cheap spell: Lava Dart, Gut Shot (paid with 2 life) or Manamorphose. That's three instants or sorceries in one turn, so at the start of combat all three Phoenixes come back with haste for 9 flying damage. The next turn, any three cheap spells bring back the ones that died.

**What Flow State does:** Brainstorm, Ponder, Faithless Looting and the free spells quickly fill your graveyard with both an instant and a sorcery. Once they're there, Flow State draws two cards, and it also counts as one of the three spells for Phoenix. Faithless Looting is a second way to get Phoenix into the graveyard: draw two, discard a Phoenix, and flashing it back counts as another spell.

**Speed, honestly:**
- **Turn 1 or 2:** A black land plus Lotus Petal, Dark Ritual, Buried Alive and Lava Dart is a turn-1 kill. A turn-2 kill is more realistic.
- **Odds:** You'll have Buried Alive or Looting plus a black source by turn 2 about 65% of the time from natural draws alone, before Brainstorm and Ponder dig for more.
- **Exact line:** The checker gives under 1% for drawing every card in the exact line I listed by turn 3. That's because it counts specific cards, and the deck has plenty of substitutes for each piece.

**Directions I considered:**
1. A Grixis combo deck that borrows Reanimator's fast mana and discard (Dark Ritual, Lotus Petal, Thoughtseize).
2. An Izzet Tempo shell with Phoenix as one more threat and Buried Alive splashed in.

results.prompt: Brew me a Pauper deck built around Ardent Recruit, Search Party Captain and Springleaf Drum.
results.text:
I built a Boros artifact-aggro brew around the three cards. No published list has run Ardent Recruit, Search Party Captain and Springleaf Drum together in the last 400 days, so the mana and removal come from the Synthesizer deck (Boros artifacts with Glint Hawk and Kor Skyfisher).

**The plan:** Fill turns 1–2 with cheap creatures and artifacts. Ancient Den, Great Furnace, Rustvale Bridge, the Drum, Clues from the Inspectors, Blood tokens from Voldaren Epicure and Relic of Progenitus all count toward the three artifacts that make Ardent Recruit a 3/3 and Galvanic Blast deal 4 damage.

- **Search Party Captain:** costs 1 less for each creature you attacked with this turn. After attacking with two or three creatures, it comes down after combat for one or two mana and draws a card.
- **Springleaf Drum:** taps creatures that can't attack yet ("summoning-sick") for mana of any color. Glint Hawk and Kor Skyfisher can return it to your hand to recast.
- **Finishing:** 4 Lightning Bolt and 4 Galvanic Blast clear blockers or burn the opponent out.

**Directions I considered:**
1. Mono-White, borrowing the Mono-White Aggro package (Battle Screech, Inspectors).
2. Orzhov (white-black), borrowing the Glintblade deck's Cast Down.
3. Boros (red-white), borrowing the Synthesizer deck's mana and burn.

I chose Boros because Galvanic Blast is the strongest metalcraft payoff besides Recruit, and Bolt gives an aggro deck the reach it needs.

**How the cards fit:**
- **Requested cards:** 4 copies each.
- **Captain enablers:** 20 cheap creatures, almost all one- and two-drops.
- **Artifacts for metalcraft:** 25 cards, including 9 artifact lands.
- **Removal:** 3 Journey to Nowhere alongside the burn.
- **Mana:** 19 lands, in line with the Synthesizer deck's mana.
- **Sideboard:** Pyroblast/Red Elemental Blast for Terror and Faeries, Dust to Dust for Affinity and Wildfire, and Electrickery, Prismatic Strands and Destroy Evil for creature decks.

**Honest odds:** You have about a 49% chance to see Ardent Recruit by turn 3, and the same for the Drum. The exact 7-card sequence I submitted as the "win line" is only an example: every card in it shows up by turn 6 in under 1% of games. The deck works through overlap instead: any mix of cheap creatures and artifacts turns on Captain and metalcraft.

results.prompt: Brew me a Pauper deck built around Aurora Eidolon, Sandstorm Eidolon and Spirit Mascot.
results.text:
I built a Boros (red-white) graveyard-value aggro deck, and it's a brew. No published list in the last 400 days plays these three cards together.

**How the cards work together**
- **The Eidolons:** Each one returns from your graveyard to your hand whenever you cast a multicolored spell.
- **Spirit Mascot:** It's a red-white card, so it's a multicolored spell itself. It gets a +1/+1 counter every time cards leave your graveyard.
- **Discarding instead of paying 4:** You rarely pay 4 mana for an Eidolon at the start. You discard them with Faithless Looting, Thrilling Discovery or Pursue the Past.
- **Bringing them back:** Cheap two-color spells return them, and each return grows Mascot. Those spells are Thrilling Discovery, Pursue the Past and Wojek Halberdiers, plus Mascot itself.
- **Using them as reusable tools:**
  - Sandstorm Eidolon: pay {R} and sacrifice it, and a creature can't block this turn.
  - Aurora Eidolon: pay {W} and sacrifice it to prevent 3 damage, such as a Bolt or a blocker's hit.
  - Either one comes back on your next multicolored spell.
- **More ways to grow Mascot:** Flashback casts (Looting, Pursue the Past, Rally the Peasants, Battle Screech) and Lunarch Veteran's disturb all cast cards from the graveyard, so they also grow Mascot.
- **The finish:** Rally the Peasants, then its flashback, gives your team +4 power in one attack.

**Three directions I considered**
1. **Mono-Red Rally with a white splash:** Burning-Tree Emissary and Manamorphose count as multicolored. But almost none of its cards return the Eidolons, grow Mascot or use the graveyard.
2. **Grindy Pursue the Past control:** It recurs Eidolons well, but it has no real way to win.
3. **The Boros Aggro shell (my pick):** This is the closest match to the Mono-White Aggro deck on your list. It already runs Thrilling Discovery, Faithless Looting, Rally the Peasants and Battle Screech. That means its discard outlets, flashback cards and multicolored card draw already do both jobs the Eidolons and Mascot need.

**Honest numbers**
- You see Spirit Mascot by turn 3 about 49% of the time, and a discard card about 86%. Both together is about 41%.
- The deck wins around turn 6.
- The exact combo I described, with every named card drawn by turn 6, only happens about 2% of the time. Read it as a typical game, not a fixed combo. Many cards in the deck can fill each step.

**Mana:** 19 lands (14 white sources, 11 red), which follows the Boros Aggro lists. The checker flagged that those lists run about 16 white sources, versus my 14. I added an extra Plains to close some of that gap.

**Sideboard (aimed at the top decks):**
- Prismatic Strands, Electrickery and Fire at Will against Madness and Elves.
- Red Elemental Blast and Pyroblast against Terror.
- Dust to Dust against Affinity and Wildfire.
- Journey to Nowhere and Thraben Charm as flexible answers. Thraben Charm also exiles graveyards; I kept graveyard hate out of the main deck because this deck needs its own graveyard.

results.prompt: Brew me a Premodern deck built around Future Sight, Academy Rector and Veteran Explorer.
results.text:
I built a four-color (green, white, blue, red) Survival toolbox brew. No published list runs Future Sight, Academy Rector and Veteran Explorer together. The only real list with Rector and Explorer is Pattern Combo, a Survival of the Fittest deck that uses Goblin Bombardment as its sacrifice outlet. I borrowed its creature package and mana base, cut black, and added blue for Future Sight.

**The plan:** Veteran Explorer and Academy Rector are mana and tutoring that you trigger yourself by sacrificing them to Goblin Bombardment.
- **Turn 1:** Birds of Paradise.
- **Turn 2:** Veteran Explorer and Survival of the Fittest.
- **Turn 3:** Cast Bombardment and sacrifice Explorer. Both players fetch two basic lands, and they come in untapped, so you have mana to cast Rector right away. Then sacrifice Rector to put Future Sight onto the battlefield a turn before you could cast it.
- **After that:** Future Sight lets you play lands and spells off the top of your library. Survival finds Deranged Hermit, whose four squirrels feed Bombardment, and Karmic Guide brings Hermit back for the kill around turn 6.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **This one:** borrowing the Survival/Bombardment package that Pattern Combo, Tradewind Survival and Cradle Control all use.
2. **Living Death (black-green):** most Explorer lists are this deck, but adding white and blue for Rector and Future Sight would stretch it to five colors.
3. **Enchantress-style:** Rector fetching Opalescence or Replenish, but Explorer does nothing there.

I picked the first because Bombardment is the one card that lets both death triggers happen exactly when you want them, and it also wins the game.

**Honest notes:**
- **The fast turn-3 line is rare.** The odds tool puts the chance of having Explorer, Bombardment or Enlightened Tutor, and Rector or Survival all by turn 4 at about 23%. That doesn't count Survival tutoring for missing pieces, or Rector and Explorer dying in combat or to the opponent's removal. Without that line, the deck plays as a slower value deck.
- **Explorer ramps your opponent too.** Each player gets two basics, so sacrifice it when you can use the mana right away.
- **Future Sight runs 3 copies, not 4.** A second copy does nothing, and 4 Rector plus 2 Enlightened Tutor act as extra copies. Enlightened Tutor puts a card on top of your library, and with Future Sight out you can then cast it.
- **Turn 6 is a target, not a promise.** The checker gives a 0% chance of having naturally drawn every card in the win line by turn 6. That's expected: the line relies on Survival, Rector and Enlightened Tutor to find its pieces, and the checker doesn't simulate tutors.
- **Why no blue staples:** I left out Counterspell, Impulse, Gush and the other blue cards the checker suggested on purpose. Blue is only here for Future Sight, and the slots go to creatures that Survival and Bombardment need.
- **Sideboard:** aimed at the current top decks. Hydroblast, Circle of Protection: Red and Spike Feeder are for Sligh and Goblins, Pyroblast and Uktabi Orangutan for Stiflenought, and Seal of Cleansing, Monk Realist and Annul for Enchantress and Replenish.

results.prompt: Brew me a Premodern deck built around Utopia Tree, Rhystic Tutor and Bloodfire Colossus.
results.text:
I built a three-color (black, red, green) Survival Reanimator deck, and it's a brew. No published list in the last 400 days plays all three of your cards together.

**The plan:** Birds of Paradise and Utopia Tree ramp you into Survival of the Fittest on turn 2. Survival discards a creature to find Bloodfire Colossus, then discards the Colossus itself. Buried Alive and Wild Mongrel also put a Colossus in the graveyard. On turn 3, Exhume or Animate Dead brings it back without paying 8 mana. It attacks for 6 a turn, and Recurring Nightmare can return a second Colossus. You finish with Colossus's ability: {R}, sacrifice it, 6 damage to each creature and each player. That blast also wipes the board against Goblins, Sligh and Zoo, and kills whatever creature Exhume handed your opponent.

**What each requested card does:**
- **Utopia Tree:** makes any color for three colors, it's discard fodder for Survival and something to sacrifice for Recurring Nightmare or Cabal Therapy's flashback, and it pays the {R} for the blast.
- **Rhystic Tutor:** works as extra copies of Survival, a reanimation spell or Buried Alive.
- **Bloodfire Colossus:** the only big creature in the deck, so it's your threat, your board wipe and your finisher.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **Hermit Druid combo** (the format's Hermit Druid deck, using Tree as an extra Birds). Colossus adds nothing to how that deck wins.
2. **Red-green ramp with Sneak Attack**, splashing black for the Tutor. A Colossus put in with Sneak Attack only deals 12 (attack for 6, blast for 6), so you'd need two in hand to kill.
3. **Survival Reanimator.** I took the Survival, Recurring Nightmare and mana-creature package from the black-green Survival deck and Exhume and Animate Dead from Reanimator.

I chose the third because it's the only one where all three cards actually move the game toward a win.

**Honest odds and limits:**
- On the play, with no mulligan, you have both a way to bin the Colossus and a reanimation spell by turn 4 about 71% of the time.
- The blast hits you for 6 too, so only fire it once the Colossus has attacked a few times or when it kills your opponent.
- Animate Dead gives the Colossus -1/-0, so it attacks for 5.
- Your opponent can pay {2} to stop Rhystic Tutor. Fast control decks like Stiflenought often will, which makes it the deck's weakest card. It's in because you asked for it.

**Sideboard:** Pyroblast for Stiflenought, Smother, Engineered Plague and Lightning Bolt for Goblins and Sligh, and Naturalize and Uktabi Orangutan for Enchantress, Replenish and Stasis. Two Sneak Attack are the backup plan against graveyard hate, and Withered Wretch is graveyard hate of your own for other graveyard decks.
